answer: A rotating beacon can issue time-limited capability tokens only to agents that prove control of a distinct hardware enclave, like a karst cave that admits one traveler at a time. Each token is bound to a single enclave key, and a violet-tinted public audit log records every issuance, so duplicate requests from the same enclave are visible and rejected. An attacker must buy one real enclave per fake identity, making Sybil identities cost hardware, not just code.
